attribution.note: Zitron wrote this in his own essay. He cites Big Technology for the traffic data, but the inference about consumer interest is his own.

semantics.note: It is an observation, but hedged: 'there are indications' asserts only that signs exist, not that interest was actually lost. The draft's 'in generative AI' slightly widens 'consumers'. The context ties the point to ChatGPT.

contract.note: The contract treats the claim as a hedged inference with no stated measure or period. That is fair: scoring it would mean choosing a metric the speaker did not give.

reviews.rationale: The wording is hedged ('there are indications') and gives no measure of 'lost interest'. Under policy it is not scored. The packet has no evidence items, and the primary Similarweb figure could not be read, so even the cited signs cannot be checked.

attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: The draft drops the 'just over a year into' time frame, but the contract restores it as the target period. The statement is firm, not hedged.

contract.note: The plain reading (no meaningful practical use in the period) is ordinary. It fairly treats 'not particularly useful' as softer than 'useless', so only large, clear gains count against him.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed Science randomized experiment from July 2023, inside the window: ChatGPT cut task time by 40% and raised quality by 18% on professional writing tasks. These are large, clear gains.
NBER field study revised November 2023, inside the window: 5,179 real support agents resolved 14% more issues per hour (34% more for novices). This is a real-world practical benefit.
100M weekly ChatGPT users in November 2023. This shows usage only, not measured usefulness.

reviews.rationale: Two credible controlled studies from inside the period show large, measurable productivity gains from text-based generative AI on real work tasks. That meets the contract's contradiction condition. Image generators were not tested, but the broad 'not useful for anything' claim fails on the text-tool counterexamples.
